name: Question 3
problem:
By integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 3,\,-1\le z\le 1}.$
worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy\,dx\,dz
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $x,$ and then $z,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}z+\frac{1}{y}\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{2}zy+\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|]_{y=1}^{y=3}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}z(3-1)+(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-0)\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}z+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{x}^{2}z+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}2z{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{2}{3}\,z{x}^{3}+x\operatorname{ln}⁡3]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{2}{3}\,z(8-0)+(2-0)\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{16}{3}\,z+2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{16}{3}z+2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,dz & ={[\frac{8}{3}{z}^{2}+2z\operatorname{ln}⁡3]}_{z=-1}^{z=1} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}(1-1)+2(1-(-1))\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

a
3ln⁡2
b
4ln⁡3
c
2ln⁡3
d
3−2ln⁡2
e
2−ln⁡3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral: ∭Rx2z+1ydV=∫−11∫02∫13x2z+1ydydxdz

Since we're integrating first with respect to y, then x, and then z, we write dV=dydxdz.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to y, treating x and z as constants: ∫−11∫02∫13x2z+1ydydxdz=∫−11∫02[∫13x2z+1ydy]dxdz=∫−11∫02[x2zy+ln⁡|y|]y=1y=3dxdz=∫−11∫02x2z(3−1)+(ln⁡3−0)dxdz=∫−11∫022x2z+ln⁡3dxdz

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to x, treating z as a constant: ∫−11∫022x2z+ln⁡3dxdz=∫−11[∫022zx2+ln⁡3dx]dz=∫−11[23zx3+xln⁡3]x=0x=2dz=∫−1123z(8−0)+(2−0)ln⁡3dz=∫−11163z+2ln⁡3dz

Finally, we integrate with respect to z: ∫−11163z+2ln⁡3dz=[83z2+2zln⁡3]z=−1z=1=83(1−1)+2(1−(−1))ln⁡3=4ln⁡3
